# The tab-reorder no-flash spec's count oracle fires on the pre-drop pair under load

## Context

Gate 2 of the v13.3.1 cut (#20022), run 1 on `dev` e2f77dd0fb (full `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard`, one worker): one red at position 199 of 230, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL.spec.mjs:96` "a reorder never paints the withheld headers between the drop and the settled partition". Green alone 6 of 6 (`--repeat-each=3`). Run 2 on the same head did not hit it. The spec is #19987 → #20008's witness (a reorder painting the headers the overflow withholds); this ticket is about its oracle, not the product.

**Observed** (run 1, `expect(max(samples.count)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(settled)`): one sampled frame after the drop laid out 2 headers; the settled strip showed 1; the second assertion, no header outside the strip box, passed. The retained trace's DOM snapshots for the pane's toolbar: the pair `neo-tab-header-button-4, -5` before the drag, `-5` hidden behind the drag proxy during it, `-5` alone once settled; the overflow's withheld headers are out of the DOM (`removeDom`) at every snapshot.

**Design authority:** the spec's own docblock: "No frame may lay out more headers than the settled strip shows, and no header may paint outside the strip box." The first sentence encodes an assumption the drop breaks.

## The Problem

The strip the spec captures is unfocused, so three or two headers fit. The drop's `SortZone#processDragEnd` restores focus to the dragged header, which reveals the toolbar's focus-gated actions; they take strip width and `Overflow#project` re-partitions the strip to fewer headers (the mechanism #20020 / #20021 measured for the tab-drag headers spec). So after a drop, **settled < pre-drop** is the normal case. The count oracle compares every sampled frame with the *settled* count, so the legitimate pre-drop pair, laid out until the re-partition lands, reads as a flash. In a solo run the re-partition lands inside the first frame after the drop and no sample sees two headers; under full-run load it lands a frame or more later and the sampler catches the pair. The headers #19987 fixed (withheld ones painted) never entered the DOM.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL.spec.mjs`: `startSampler` records per frame `{count, outside}` only, so a two-header frame cannot be told apart by identity; lines 124–127 assert `samples.length > 3`, `max(count) ≤ settled`, `outside == []`.
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs` `processDragEnd`: focus restore to the dragged button after the drop.
- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`: `project` / `computeOverflow` re-partition for the usable extent once the focus-gated actions mount (their `resize` events arrive after the drop).

## The Fix

Spec-only, in `WorkstationTabReorderNoFlashNL.spec.mjs`:

- The sampler records the **ids** of the laid-out headers per frame (and keeps `outside`).
- The oracle becomes identity-based: every frame's shown ids are a subset of the union of the pre-drop visible ids and the settled visible ids. A header outside that union is a withheld header painted, the #19987 defect; the pre-drop pair laid out until the re-partition is not.
- The count comparison goes; the outside-the-box assertion stays; the sample-count floor stays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Under an injected post-drop stall (6× CPU throttling), with both oracles evaluated on one shared sample set per drop over N ≥ 5 drops, the old count rule fires in at least one drop (the settled strip narrower than the pre-drop one) while the identity rule produces no stray in any of the N; the receipt records both counts. *(Restated 2026-10-23 13:1xZ from "the old oracle fails and the repaired passes, 3 of 3": the race is probabilistic even under throttle, so the acceptance is the paired counterexample on the same samples, not a run count manufactured to a target; Euclid's review clarification on #20051.)*
- [ ] AC-2: Diagonal with teeth: with a withheld header forced into the laid-out DOM for one frame after the drop (a page-side probe that un-removes one `appliedHiddenIds` member), the repaired oracle fails naming that id.
- [ ] AC-3: Both arms of the file green alone 6 of 6 (`--repeat-each=3`) on the repaired spec, no `waitForTimeout` (`check-fixed-sleeps` green).
- [ ] AC-4: Hosted `e2e-brain` tier green on the PR head.

## Out of Scope

The product behaviour (#19987 → #20008 stands); the focus-restore re-partition itself (by design, #20020's reading); the other roving specimens of the gate (all dispositioned on #20022).

## Avoided Traps

- Relaxing the count to `pre-drop` instead of `settled`: a flash of exactly one withheld header during a pre-drop-sized frame would pass.
- Pre-focusing the strip before the capture (so settled = pre-drop): removes the unfocused-to-focused drop the test is about and the third header the #20020 class needed.
- A fixed sleep before sampling: hides the frames the test exists to watch.
